key_insight: Current vision-language models are not yet reliable enough for medical image quality assessment under common image corruptions or contextual bias.
clinical_relevance: In practice, this means automated image quality checks could be skewed by degradation, privacy-preserving edits, or patient metadata, which may affect diagnostic workflows and safety.
method: Tested 7 corruption types across 5 severity levels on MediMeta-C
Compared score changes, embedding shifts, and effects of textual metadata
evidence_signal: Across seven modalities, pixelation caused the largest score drop on average (-20.58%), while institutional prestige increased scores by +17.15% and equipment age lowered them by -14.7%.
watch_item: Because performance changes with corruption and metadata, deploying VLMs for MIQA may require strict validation to avoid biased or unstable quality judgments.
paper_title: Assessing VLM Reliability for Medical Image Quality Evaluation Under Corruption and Bias
